group.title: Technology
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A set of steps that a computer follows to solve a problem.
examples: The search {algorithm} sorts the results by relevance.
wrong: An algorithm is a kind of cable that connects two computers.

words.meaning: The amount of data that a connection can carry at one time.
examples: Video calls need a lot of {bandwidth}.
wrong: Bandwidth is the width of a computer screen.

words.meaning: Software or hardware that blocks unwanted access to a network.
examples: The {firewall} stopped the unknown connection.
wrong: A firewall is a wall that protects a building from a fire.

words.meaning: The process of turning information into a code so others cannot read it.
examples: {Encryption} keeps our messages private.
wrong: Encryption is the process of making a file larger on purpose.

words.meaning: Computers on the internet that store data and run programs for you.
examples: I saved the photos to the {cloud}.
wrong: The cloud is a folder that exists only on one broken laptop.

words.meaning: An organized collection of data stored so that it can be found quickly.
examples: The customer’s address is stored in the {database}.
wrong: A database is a program for editing photographs.

words.meaning: The part of a program that a person sees and uses.
examples: The app has a clean and simple {interface}.
wrong: An interface is a battery that powers the device.

words.meaning: To make software newer by adding changes or fixes.
examples: Please {update} the app before you log in.
wrong: You update an app by deleting it from the phone.

words.meaning: A copy of data kept in case the original is lost.
examples: Make a {backup} before you reinstall the system.
wrong: A backup is the original file that you must never copy.

words.meaning: To find and remove errors in a program.
examples: It took two days to {debug} the code.
wrong: To debug a program, you add as many errors as possible.

words.meaning: To put software into use so that people can run it.
examples: The team will {deploy} the new version tonight.
wrong: You deploy a program by switching off the computer for good.

words.meaning: A computer that stores data or services for other computers to use.
examples: The website went down when the {server} crashed.
wrong: A server is a person who brings food in a restaurant, not a computer.

words.meaning: A group of computers and devices that are connected to share information.
examples: The office {network} is down again.
wrong: A network is one single device that is not connected to anything.

words.meaning: A program used to look at pages on the internet.
examples: Open the link in your {browser}.
wrong: A browser is a machine that prints documents.

words.meaning: To send a file from your device to the internet.
examples: Please {upload} your photo to the form.
wrong: You upload a file by saving it only on your own device.

words.meaning: Software made to damage a computer or steal information.
examples: The email contained {malware}.
wrong: Malware is a helpful program that cleans your computer.

words.meaning: Sending false messages to trick people into giving away private information.
examples: The email was a {phishing} attempt to steal my password.
wrong: Phishing is a sport in which people catch fish with a net.

words.meaning: The delay between sending a signal and getting a response.
examples: High {latency} makes online games feel slow.
wrong: Latency is the speed at which a printer prints a page.

words.meaning: Describing software whose code anyone may read, use and change.
examples: The tool is {open-source}, so anyone can improve it.
wrong: Open-source software has code that no one is allowed to see.

words.meaning: An early model of a product used to test an idea.
examples: The team built a {prototype} before making the final app.
wrong: A prototype is the last version that customers receive.

words.meaning: To make data on different devices match each other.
examples: Your notes {sync} between your phone and your laptop.
wrong: Two devices sync when each one deletes all of its files.

words.meaning: A small program that adds a feature to a larger program.
examples: I installed a {plugin} to check my spelling.
wrong: A plugin is the largest part of the program, and nothing works without it.

words.meaning: The process of proving who you are before you are allowed in.
examples: Two-step {authentication} protects your account.
wrong: Authentication is the process of deleting an old account.

words.meaning: A place where a device stores data so it can load faster next time.
examples: Clear your {cache} if the page looks wrong.
wrong: A cache is a tool that stops a device from storing any data.

words.meaning: A short program that automates a simple task.
examples: I wrote a {script} to rename all the files.
wrong: A script is a screen that stops the computer from working.

words.meaning: The physical parts of a computer, such as the screen and keyboard.
examples: We bought new {hardware} for the office.
wrong: Hardware is the set of programs that run inside a computer.

words.meaning: Computer systems that do tasks that normally need human thinking.
examples: {Artificial intelligence} can translate speech into text.
wrong: Artificial intelligence is a person who repairs computers by hand.

words.meaning: A screen that shows the most important information in one place.
examples: The {dashboard} shows sales for each region.
wrong: A dashboard is the password you type to open a program.

words.meaning: Programs that tell a computer what to do.
examples: The {software} lets you edit photos.
wrong: Software is the set of physical parts inside a computer.

words.meaning: Working without wires or cables.
examples: We use a {wireless} connection at the office.
wrong: A wireless mouse must be connected with a long cable.
